topic: Move Semantics and Rvalue References in C++
explanation: Move semantics in C++ enable efficient transfer of resources from temporary objects (rvalues) to new objects, minimizing unnecessary copying. Rvalue references (denoted by &&) allow functions to distinguish between lvalues and rvalues, facilitating resource transfer and optimization. This feature is essential for modern C++ programming to improve performance, especially when dealing with resource-intensive objects like containers, smart pointers, and user-defined types.
code_example: // Use move semantics to take ownership of buf's resources
processBuffer(std::move(buf1)); // Passing an rvalue to invoke move semantics
example_explanation: This example demonstrates move semantics by defining a Buffer class with copy and move constructors. The function processBuffer accepts an rvalue reference to a Buffer object, allowing it to efficiently transfer resources using std::move. In main(), std::move(buf1) converts buf1 into an rvalue, enabling processBuffer to invoke the move constructor instead of copying. This showcases how rvalue references and move semantics optimize resource management in modern C++.
